meta.purpose: Timestamps, counts, units, hints, table data on the board, toast meta.

label.purpose: Names, group headings, badges, chips, small buttons, menu items, segment labels.

body.purpose: Sentences, descriptions, alert text, prose; running text measures 60 to 72ch.

prose.purpose: Transcript prose and rendered markdown, Figtree at 1.55.

title.purpose: Page, dialog and empty-state titles; 18px at 390px to 20px at 1024px.

kpi.purpose: A stat tile's figure, tabular; 20px to 24px, the title size under 900px.

column-head.purpose: A ledger's header band, uppercase, 0.06em tracking.

code.purpose: JetBrains Mono for code, commands, paths, tool names and keycaps; ligatures off.

display.purpose: Fredoka 600, brand display only: marketing, a brand moment in an empty state. Never product chrome; the wordmark is Nunito.

shadows.name: shadow-xs
shadows.purpose: Inputs, select triggers, the new-session prompt.

shadows.name: shadow-tile
shadows.value: 0 1px 2px light-dark(oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.07), oklch(0% 0 0 / 0.3)), 0 0 0 1px light-dark(oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.035), oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.06))
shadows.purpose: Cards, tiles, icon tiles, report cards, the fluid-tabs segment.

shadows.name: shadow-raised
shadows.purpose: A thumb in a groove; the night ring edges it at night.

shadows.name: shadow-hairline
shadows.purpose: A drop under a tile with no ring: the stat tile (light), the permission card.

shadows.name: shadow-stat
shadows.purpose: The stat tile's lift: a drop below the card, ringed at night.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Tailwind ladder step.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Tailwind ladder step (meters' hover cards).

shadows.name: shadow-xl
shadows.purpose: Tailwind ladder step (project popover, tool matrix).

shadows.name: shadow-overlay
shadows.purpose: Popovers, menus, the dialog tray, toasts, floating tags (also --shadow-modal).

shadows.name: shadow-overlay-hung
shadows.purpose: A hanging surface whose top shows its own surface across the cut into its anchor (Caw's panel, kit-hang): the overlay's drop without the night ring, which would draw across the cut as a seam.

shadows.name: shadow-modal
shadows.purpose: The modal: the overlay value.

shadows.name: shadow-drawer
shadows.purpose: Sheets and drawers.

shadows.name: shadow-drop
shadows.purpose: A drawn shape's drop (the grown composer), drawn as the SVG's own feDropShadow filters so it follows the shape, not a box, and is painted once rather than reapplied as the shape moves (grown.ts): this far layer, then shadow-drop-near.

shadows.name: shadow-drop-near
shadows.purpose: The near layer of a drawn shape's drop, under shadow-drop (the grown composer, once it stands still).

shadows.name: shadow-tab-start
shadows.purpose: A folder tab's edge on the tab behind it, at its leading side: one-sided, never above its top (PaneTabs .shade).

shadows.name: shadow-tab-end
shadows.purpose: A folder tab's edge on the tab behind it, at its trailing side (PaneTabs .shade).

shadows.name: shadow-tab-start-chosen
shadows.purpose: The chosen folder tab's edge on the tab behind it, at its leading side (PaneTabs .shade).

shadows.name: shadow-tab-end-chosen
shadows.purpose: The chosen folder tab's edge on the tab behind it, at its trailing side (PaneTabs .shade).

shadows.name: shadow-inset-sel
shadows.purpose: A selected control sunk into its field (markdown editor).

shadows.name: surface-shadow-1
shadows.purpose: Shadow per surface level, paired with --surface-1…8.

shadows.name: surface-shadow-2
shadows.purpose: Step 2 of the nested elevation ladder, with surface-2; the dashboard draws the named roles instead.

shadows.name: surface-shadow-3
shadows.purpose: Step 3 of the nested elevation ladder, with surface-3; the dashboard draws the named roles instead.

shadows.name: surface-shadow-4
shadows.purpose: Step 4 of the nested elevation ladder, with surface-4; the dashboard draws the named roles instead.

shadows.name: surface-shadow-5
shadows.purpose: Step 5 of the nested elevation ladder, with surface-5; the dashboard draws the named roles instead.

shadows.name: surface-shadow-6
shadows.purpose: Step 6 of the nested elevation ladder, with surface-6; the dashboard draws the named roles instead.

shadows.name: surface-shadow-7
shadows.purpose: Step 7 of the nested elevation ladder, with surface-7; the dashboard draws the named roles instead.

shadows.name: surface-shadow-8
shadows.purpose: Step 8 of the nested elevation ladder, with surface-8; the dashboard draws the named roles instead.

shadows.name: action-ring
shadows.purpose: The action's edge: a white top hairline and a coral-tinted drop.

shadows.name: code-ring
shadows.purpose: Inner vermillion ring and soft inner glow on code blocks.

shadows.name: selected-shadow
shadows.purpose: A selected item casts nothing: selection is a fill, never a lift.

shadows.name: shadow-knob
shadows.value: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--neutral-8), 0 1px 3px var(--shadow-tint), 0 1px 1px var(--shadow-tint), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--night-ring)
shadows.purpose: The effort knob's and Browse's lifted block: a neutral-8 inner edge over shadow-raised's layers (DESIGN.md Effort chip).

shadows.name: shadow-tint
shadows.value: light-dark(oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.09), oklch(from var(--neutral-1) l c h / 0.55))
shadows.purpose: Elevation tints: warm ink by day, the deepest surface at night, never rgba black.

shadows.name: shadow-tint-2
shadows.value: light-dark(oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.14), oklch(from var(--neutral-1) l c h / 0.66))
shadows.purpose: Second shadow tint.

shadows.name: shadow-tint-3
shadows.value: light-dark(oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.2), oklch(from var(--neutral-1) l c h / 0.76))
shadows.purpose: Third shadow tint, for overlays and drawers.

shadows.name: night-ring
shadows.value: light-dark(transparent, oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.07))
shadows.purpose: At night every raised shadow adds a 1px inner ring of ink.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.value: oklch(from var(--background) l c h / var(--scrim-mix))
shadows.purpose: What a dialog's backdrop paints: the page itself, translucent.

shadows.name: material-panel
shadows.purpose: Chrome materials: structural translucency, never decoration.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Entrances, exits and changes in place.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Movement on screen: rows sliding, thumbs gliding, height tweens.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: Popovers, sheets, page swaps, shared-element flights, container morphs.

motion.name: ease-crossfade
motion.purpose: Two states trading places where they stand: a folder tab's choice over dur-settle. At most 7.2% of a change in any 1/60s at 400ms.

motion.name: ease-arrive
motion.purpose: A small mark arriving beside what it belongs to: the compaction divider's chevron.

motion.name: ease-figure
motion.purpose: A strategy figure's travel and growth (Configure → Accounts): a session riding into its lane, a bar filling, a lane reordering. The owner's reference motion, from the Projects mockups (mocks/project-paths).

motion.name: ease-goo
motion.purpose: A shape pouring out of another as one drawn silhouette (goo-join): a comment's card out of its pill. It overshoots a little and settles, the liquid's give. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its open curve (--pv3i).

motion.name: ease-goo-exit
motion.purpose: A comment's card drawn back into its pill as one silhouette, over --dur-goo-exit, and the dip its pin takes as it closes, over --dur-goo-settle. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its close curve and its anticipation's (--pv34, --pv2n).

motion.name: ease-goo-content
motion.purpose: What stands on a goo shape (a comment card's thread, its pin's figure) fading in and out as the shape pours and drains, over --dur-goo-content and --dur-goo-content-exit. CSS ease, the curve transitions.dev Gooey plus menu gives its items' icons.

motion.name: ease-glide-in
motion.purpose: A glide's first stretch (--space-3): speed rising evenly from rest into the steady pace an opening tree's line, its room and the rows under it travel at.

motion.name: ease-glide-out
motion.purpose: A glide's last stretch (--space-1): speed falling evenly from the steady pace to rest.

motion.name: dur-stagger
motion.purpose: Between one row of an opening tree and the next: its line reaches each glyph in turn at a steady pace.

motion.name: dur-cascade
motion.purpose: The most an opening tree's line takes to reach its last row: a longer tree's rows come closer together.

motion.name: dur-ghost
motion.purpose: The hover ghost gliding from row to row.

motion.name: dur-control
motion.purpose: Control colour changes, cross-fades, glyph swaps, reduced-motion page fade.

motion.name: dur-menu
motion.purpose: Tooltips, content fading into an opened place, a new thinking step.

motion.name: dur-peek
motion.purpose: How long the pointer rests on a comment's pill before its peek comes; one within this of the last goes at once (DESIGN.md, A pin's pill).

motion.name: dur-toggle
motion.purpose: A switch's knob, a checkbox's tick drawing, a step connector drawing.

motion.name: dur-exit
motion.purpose: Every exit: popovers, dialogs, sheets, toasts, floating tags, row fades.

motion.name: dur-morph
motion.purpose: A button's width following its label while it works; folding a long draft.

motion.name: dur-rail
motion.purpose: A transcript row's place opening, its rail drawing down with it.

motion.name: dur-fade
motion.purpose: Fades that carry state in place: the theme wash, a toast stack closing up.

motion.name: dur-mark-hold
motion.purpose: The longest a transcript that opens on a compaction holds its reveal for Caw's mark to be drawn. A bound, not a pace.

motion.name: dur-wait-grace
motion.purpose: How long a wait runs before its loading state (Caw at loading or reconnecting) appears; a shorter wait shows its plain surface. NN/g, Response Times: no special feedback is needed for delays under 1.0 second.

motion.name: dur-pop
motion.purpose: Floating surfaces opening, list arrivals, the live tail's height tween.

motion.name: dur-panel
motion.purpose: Dialogs and sheets entering, list movement, toasts rising, badge tint changes.

motion.name: dur-pick-up
motion.purpose: A pane card picked up off the deck: the lift's scale, sixty percent of the panel's beat, derived from it the way the breath is.

motion.name: dur-grow
motion.purpose: The composer growing up out of its pill: into the recall wheel, or by the one row that says a queued message is being edited.

motion.name: dur-grow-exit
motion.purpose: The grown composer folding back into its pill, shorter than its growth.

motion.name: dur-goo
motion.purpose: A comment's card pouring out of its pill as one silhouette, on --ease-goo. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its open (--pv3x).

motion.name: dur-goo-exit
motion.purpose: A comment's card drawn back into its pill as one silhouette, on --ease-goo-exit, shorter than its open. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its close (--pv3g).

motion.name: dur-goo-content
motion.purpose: What stands on a goo shape fading in, on --ease-goo-content after --dur-goo-content-delay. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its items' icons in (180ms; their 2px blur is left out: a transitioned filter can hang WebKit).

motion.name: dur-goo-content-delay
motion.purpose: How long what stands on a goo shape waits as the shape pours out before it resolves in: the shape has most of its room by then. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its items' icons (+120ms).

motion.name: dur-goo-content-exit
motion.purpose: What stands on a goo shape fading out as the shape drains, at once, on --ease-goo-content. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its items' icons out (120ms).

motion.name: dur-goo-settle
motion.purpose: The dip a goo shape's anchor takes as what poured out of it drains back: down --goo-dip at 30% and home, on --ease-goo-exit. A comment's pin as its card closes. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its anticipation (--pv2w).

motion.name: dur-lift
motion.purpose: A queued message's words flying between its bubble and the composer field, either way, two copies crossfading on the drawer curve.

motion.name: dur-press-hold
motion.purpose: How long a touch rests on the composer, keyboard down, before the recall wheel comes up under it.

motion.name: dur-settle
motion.purpose: The existing motion/spring.ts response for non-paging surface settlement. Paging uses UIScrollView's system mechanics. Also a folder tab's choice, on ease-crossfade (the owner's pick, "Slow · 400ms").

motion.name: dur-reveal
motion.purpose: A disclosure growing open (collapsible-content); it folds shut over --dur-exit.

motion.name: dur-hold
motion.purpose: How long a done state (a copied or saved check) stays up.

motion.name: dur-loop
motion.purpose: One turn of an ambient loop while something is pending: spinners, the task ring, and Tailwind's animate-spin (linear), animate-pulse (ease-in-out) and animate-ping (ease-out). The skeleton pulses on its own --dur-skeleton-pulse (1s), transitions.dev's recipe.

motion.name: dur-skeleton-pulse
motion.purpose: One pulse of a skeleton while it waits: its opacity from 1 down to --skeleton-pulse-floor and back, on --ease-crossfade, looping until what it stands for arrives. transitions.dev Skeleton loader and reveal, --pulse-dur: 1000ms (the owner's pick: "transitions.dev exactly").

motion.name: dur-skeleton-reveal
motion.purpose: A skeleton handing its place to what it stood for: the skeleton fades out and blurs to --skeleton-reveal-blur while the content fades in out of it, both on --ease-crossfade. transitions.dev Skeleton loader and reveal, --reveal-dur: 400ms.

motion.name: c-500
motion.purpose: Base unit for --breath.

motion.name: breath
motion.purpose: The opacity pulse of live work: beats, the in-flight tool glyph, the Working glyph, shimmer.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Every press scale, over --dur-toggle on ease-out; also the new-session dialog's exit scale and the phone deck's pick-up.

motion.name: leave-scale
motion.purpose: How far Caw shrinks as he fades out, from any drawing, over --dur-fade on ease-out, and the size a Caw whose status has no drawn enter fades in from, over --dur-pop. Material 3, Easing and duration: exit transitions are faster than enters, 200ms.

motion.name: pop-scale
motion.purpose: The scale a floating surface, chip or pop grows from and shrinks to.

motion.name: deck-step
motion.purpose: How far each card of a session mark's deck shows below the one in front (SessionMark).

motion.name: deck-shrink
motion.purpose: How much smaller each deck card is than the one in front: card i is the tile scaled by 1 - 0.11 x i.

motion.name: deck-shade-step
motion.purpose: How much more of the deck's shade each card behind takes.

motion.name: echo-scale
motion.purpose: How far a working session's echo grows from its tile before it has faded (motion/echo).

motion.name: echo-opacity
motion.purpose: A working session's echo as it leaves the tile.

motion.name: breath-floor
motion.purpose: The opacity live work breathes down to, half a breath in (the shared `breath` keyframes, app.css). The lowest at which every breather's ink (the status-live glyph, each tool family's ink, the muted ink) holds 3:1 (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11, unrounded) on every surface it stands on: page, raised, recess, recess-deep and well (probe breath-and-head). By day 0.8 (the search tool's ink on recess-deep the floor, 3.13:1); at night 0.58 (the plan tool's ink on raised the floor, 3.14:1).

motion.name: account-week-mix
motion.purpose: How far an account's week rim is mixed from its hue toward account-week-toward: a clearly different lightness of the same hue. By day 0.32 (the rim 1.9:1 or more from the disc); at night 0.63, the lowest at which the rim stands 1.8:1 from the disc for every account hue (rose the floor), the rim then 7.9:1 or more on its track.

motion.name: account-stale-opacity
motion.purpose: An account whose reading is out of date: its rings and its relay band draw at this opacity, the lowest at which every account hue holds 3:1 against the border-control track it lies on, in both schemes (by day cyan and green set the floor at 0.82, at night rose at 0.80); on the raised surface they hold more.

motion.name: ride-fade
motion.purpose: The first stretch of its nesting line over which a child's icon fades in as it leaves its parent's (motion/branch).

motion.name: pop-rise
motion.purpose: How far a floating surface or toast travels from its edge.

motion.name: fold-blur
motion.purpose: How soft a fold's content is while it folds shut or opens (Caw's panel: the update's notes, the logins signed in everywhere). transitions-dev Accordion expand: the inner panel cross-blurs 2px as its grid row goes 0fr to 1fr.

motion.name: part-blur
motion.purpose: How far out of focus the grown composer's parts come up from, and sink back into as it folds: an ask card's title, body and foot; the queued edit's label, hints and Keep it. Web only.

motion.name: goo-join
motion.purpose: Where a goo shape meets what poured out of it (a comment's pin and its card): the radius every inward corner of the one silhouette is rounded to, so the join flares out along the card's edge and the two read as one shape. A card's own corner, so the flare and the corners are one curve family.

motion.name: goo-dip
motion.purpose: How far a goo shape's anchor dips as what poured out of it drains back, over --dur-goo-settle. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu (--pv49: 5px).

motion.name: skeleton-pulse-floor
motion.purpose: The opacity a skeleton pulses down to, half a pulse in. transitions.dev Skeleton loader and reveal, --pulse-min: 0.5.

motion.name: skeleton-reveal-blur
motion.purpose: How soft a skeleton is as it goes and its content as it comes, at the far end of the reveal's cross-fade. transitions.dev Skeleton loader and reveal, --reveal-blur: 2px.

motion.name: transition-control
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), --tw-gradient-from var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), --tw-gradient-to var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: The default control transition.

motion.name: transition-fade-show
motion.purpose: Something stepping back in: its fade, and its visibility back at once (the composer's prompts, slots and controls when an ask lets go).

motion.name: transition-fade-hide
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out), visibility 0s linear var(--dur-fade)
motion.purpose: Something stepping aside: its fade, and its visibility gone once the fade is done (the composer's parts under an ask, a drawing, a minimized pill).

motion.name: transition-exit-show
motion.purpose: The composer's tray coming back: the exit's beat, its visibility back at once.

motion.name: transition-exit-hide
motion.purpose: The composer's tray leaving: the exit's beat, its visibility gone once the fade is done.

motion.name: transition-fade-blur
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out), filter var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A part fading up out of a slight blur (part-blur) in place, with reduced motion: an ask card's title, body and foot; the queued edit's label, hints and Keep it. Tested in iOS 27.2 Safari on 2026-10-23 (probe-kit ios-safari-motion): the page answers through it and the blur runs.

motion.name: transition-fade-slide-blur
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out), translate var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-drawer), filter var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A part fading up out of a slight blur (part-blur) as it slides into place on the drawer curve: an ask card's title, body and foot; the queued edit's label, hints and Keep it. Tested in iOS 27.2 Safari on 2026-10-23 (probe-kit ios-safari-motion): the page answers through it and the blur runs.

motion.name: transition-tint-press
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A chip's fill and ink on the control's beat, and its press scale (transform) on the toggle's (the tree's count, a needs card's chip, a notice row).

motion.name: transition-control-press
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), --tw-gradient-from var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), --tw-gradient-to var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: transition-control, and the press's transform on the toggle's beat.

motion.name: transition-control-slide
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), translate var(--dur-exit) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: transition-control, and a swiped row's translate home on the exit's beat.

motion.name: transition-control-ring
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), box-shadow var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: transition-control, and a ring drawn as a box-shadow on the same beat.

motion.name: transition-chip-settle
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A chip whose fill and ink settle on the panel's beat, its press (transform) on the toggle's (a rollout's state chip).

motion.name: transition-pick-card
motion.value: border-color var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out), background-color var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A choice card's outline and fill on the fade's beat, its press (transform) on the control's (the account strategy picker).

motion.name: transition-frame-end-first
motion.value: inset-inline-end var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-in-out) 0ms, inset-inline-start var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-in-out) var(--dur-ghost)
motion.purpose: A frame gliding between cards: its leading edge moves at once, its trailing edge a ghost's beat later, so it stretches then settles (the channel cards).

motion.name: transition-frame-start-first
motion.value: inset-inline-start var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-in-out) 0ms, inset-inline-end var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-in-out) var(--dur-ghost)
motion.purpose: transition-frame-end-first's mirror, for a glide the other way.

motion.name: transition-split-surface
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), padding var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-drawer)
motion.purpose: A side surface sliding in beside the main pane: its fade and travel on ease-out, its room (padding) on the drawer curve.

motion.name: transition-ring-arc
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-in-out), stroke var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out), opacity var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A usage ring's arc drawing to its new length, its stroke and fade on the toggle's beat.

motion.name: transition-rail-tip
motion.value: transform var(--dur-morph) var(--ease-in-out), width var(--dur-morph) var(--ease-in-out), opacity var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A rail's selection tip gliding and resizing to its new item, fading on the control's beat.

motion.name: transition-panel-travel
motion.value: transform var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-in-out), opacity var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A panel travelling to its new place on ease-in-out while it fades on ease-out (the new-session location panels).

motion.name: transition-panel-resize
motion.value: transform var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-in-out), height var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-in-out), opacity var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A panel moving and taking its new height on the toggle's beat, fading on the control's (the model list's panel).

motion.name: transition-suggest-chip
motion.value: scale var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out), background-color var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A suggestion chip: its press on the toggle's beat, its tint and outline on the panel's, its ink on the control's.

motion.name: transition-segment
motion.value: transform var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out), width var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out), height var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out), opacity var(--dur-ghost) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A segmented control's thumb gliding and resizing to its tab, fading on the ghost's beat.

motion.name: transition-fold-fade
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-exit) var(--ease-out), filter var(--dur-exit) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A fold's inner panel fading and cross-blurring out of --fold-blur as it opens and shuts (UpdateCard, MovedLogins, RecordCard; the open state stretches it to the panel's beat). A transitioned filter can hang WebKit; these folds are each driven on WebKit by scripts/probe-kit/specs/web/safari-blurs.ts, so no other element takes this.

motion.name: transition-morph-fade
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-morph) var(--ease-out), filter var(--dur-morph) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A pending button's label and spinner cross-fading and cross-blurring as one replaces the other (the kit's pending-content), where motion is wanted. A transitioned filter can hang WebKit (scripts/probe-kit/specs/web/safari-blurs.ts); no other element takes this.

motion.name: transition-band-hide
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-exit) var(--ease-out), visibility var(--dur-exit), background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: The connection band (HubBand) going, with less motion: its fade and its visibility on the exit's beat, its tint and ink on the control's.

narrative.northStar: The Quiet Ledger, re-skinned for Caw&Co
narrative.overview:
CawCo is a board an operator glances at between other work. It answers one question: does anything need me right now? The design treats that glance like reading a departure board. Rows hold still, numbers line up, and a quiet row has to mean a healthy row. The copy is a calm operator's log, not a personality brand (Voice).

The direction (Caw&Co "3b · Coral action") keeps the shipped ledger's density, metrics, spacing, radii, motion and Solar icons, and re-skins its colour and type. The surface is warm paper by day (neutral hue ~85) and roost-dark at night (hue ~70). Chroma stays low in all chrome. Colour is spent on five things only: the coral action (where you act), status, identity marks, the coral focus ring, and data that crosses a threshold. Depth comes from a recessed frame holding raised content, not from heavy shadows. The density is set by the operator's job: 44px rows, a 32px header band, 90px stat tiles and the 14px body size.

Neither scheme is the original. The theme class on `<html>` (resolved from the reader's choice or the OS by `theme.svelte.ts`) sets `color-scheme`, and every colour token picks its side through `light-dark()`. A design is drawn and checked in both, never light-first or dark-first.

Motion is continuity, never decoration. Something that exists on both sides of a change travels to its new place rather than vanishing and reappearing, and a list that changes reflows rather than jumps. Nothing moves after it has landed unless it is live work, and live work breathes slowly. The code rejects: ease-in curves, `rgba(0,0,0,…)` shadows, weights above 500, indigo, and hue used for decoration.
keyCharacteristics: A coral action on warm paper; colour elsewhere only where it carries meaning.
The frame recesses; content sits raised on it.
Figtree for the product, JetBrains Mono for code, paths and IDs, Fredoka 600 for brand display only. Product weights 400 and 500 only.
A spacing ladder measured off the reference comps (4, 7, 11, 14, 18, 21, 25, 32), not a 4px grid.
Solar bold-duotone icons throughout, linear only for chevrons and arrows.
Motion that keeps one object on screen through every change, honours reduced motion everywhere, and exits faster than it enters.

rules.name: The No Ease-In Rule
rules.body: No ease-in curve exists. Anything that starts slow feels like the interface hesitating.

rules.name: The Fast Exit Rule
rules.body: Exits are shorter than entrances. A popover opens over 260ms and closes over 160ms. A dialog opens over 280ms and closes over 160ms. A toast rises over 280ms and leaves over 160ms.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: What is on both sides of a change travels; it never vanishes on one side and appears on the other (`motion/share.svelte.ts`). A sidebar row becomes the tab it opens, a section row's title flies into the editor header, a sent message flies from the composer into the transcript row it became. A flight runs 280ms on the drawer curve, as a transform (FLIP) or a clip that opens from the source's box. The source is hidden while its copy flies, so the screen never shows two. A surface that closes on work still running travels into the place that work is parked, and comes back out of it (The Work Outlives Its Surface Rule).

rules.name: The Nothing Jumps Rule
rules.body: When a list changes, rows that stay slide to their new places, rows that leave close while fading, and rows that arrive are uncovered top to bottom while what follows makes room (`motion/rows.svelte.ts`). Movement takes 280ms on ease-in-out, arrivals fade over 260ms, departures fade over 160ms, all started on the same frame. In a batch a tree's fold paces (closing over `--dur-exit`, opening at its line's speed), a row's fade runs over its own uncovering's or closing's duration, so each row is one clock. A move that happens entirely off screen jumps instead of sliding, so nothing drifts into view behind the reader's scroll.

rules.name: The Interruptible Rule
rules.body: Every transition turns back from where it is drawn. Popovers transition on `data-state` rather than playing keyframes, folds animate from the drawn height, and a segmented thumb caught mid-glide restarts from where it stands.

rules.name: The Stay In Context Rule
rules.body: The reader stays where they are and knows what is true, from the moment they ask for something to the moment it is done. The owner: "This fluid ux is the bar for any part of this project. Keeps the user in context." Four questions shape every flow, and their answers decide its form: Where is their attention? The flow happens there. The thing they acted on stays in view and becomes its own result. Nothing sends them to another page, stacks a second surface on the first, or leaves a toast for them to connect back to what they did. What do they need to know to decide? The consequences this action really has, shown before they commit, and nothing more. A light, reversible action just happens where it was asked. One that reaches other things names those things where the decision is made. What is true right now? The system's state as it changes, not the state the interface hopes for. Something is done when the system says it is. An action that takes time shows its progress on the things it is changing. What if it doesn't go to plan? They are still where they were, with what they had, told what happened to which thing, and able to carry on from there. Work that runs longer than the surface that started it is kept by The Work Outlives Its Surface Rule, through a reload and a dismissal alike.

rules.name: The Open Page Rule
rules.body: Almost nothing blurs the page or stops the reader acting elsewhere. A surface that asks or shows something opens in the page, beside what it concerns, and the rest of the page stays live: the reader can scroll, read, or press something else, and the surface waits or follows. The owner: "standing rule, there should almost never be a dialog or a sheet that blurs the page or prevents the user from taking other actions". The question to ask: if they press something else now, does anything break? If nothing breaks, nothing blocks. A scrim, a blur or a modal hold is for the rare moment when acting elsewhere would make the open question wrong, and the dialog, sheet and drawer recipes below are for those moments only. Add machine is one by the owner's word ("IT'S A MODAL, AND IT'S MINIMIZEABLE TO SOMEWHERE IF IT'S DISMISSED WHILE IT'S WORKING, THEN I CAN GO BACK TO WHERE I WAS"): the kit's dialog, centred over the scrim on a desk and its bottom sheet on a phone, its two ways in as tabs (Over SSH, By a command) over the details, with no question first.

rules.name: The Work Outlives Its Surface Rule
rules.body: Work started in a surface (a window, a sheet, a tray, a popover, a dialog, a drawer) that runs longer than the surface stays open (an install, a spawn, an upload, a sign-in, an update, any job of more than a few seconds) belongs to the work, not to the surface, and nothing the reader does to the page loses it. Work that is done within a second and leaves nothing behind (a rename, a toggle) is outside it: it just happens (The Stay In Context Rule).

rules.name: The Show Don't Tell Rule
rules.body: A fact with a shape is drawn, not written out: a schedule as times on a line, a budget as a meter, a run of outcomes as marks in their status colours, who runs something as their mark. Words are for what has no shape (a prompt, a reason, a name), and a row of labelled text facts is a sign that something should be drawn. The owner, on a routine's detail written as label and value rows: "walls of text with no structure, many things can be told with ui or visually rather than spamming text rows".

rules.name: The One Loop Rule
rules.body: Anything that turns or blinks while something is pending runs one ambient loop, `--dur-loop` (1.2s): a spinner, the task ring's arc, and Tailwind's `animate-spin`, `animate-pulse` and `animate-ping`, which the theme points at the token. A rotation turns linearly; a pulse runs ease-in-out and a ping ease-out. The skeleton's pulse is the one exception, the owner's pick of transitions.dev's recipe exactly: `--dur-skeleton-pulse` (1s), every skeleton on its own one clock. Longer rhythms are multiples of the breath, never new numbers: the thinking indicator's words change every two breaths. Tailwind's default transition timing (`transition-colors` and its siblings) is `--dur-control` on ease-out.

rules.name: The Steady Swap Rule
rules.body: A text swap never moves what stands beside it, and runs on one clock. Words change in place through MorphText (`components/ui/morph-text`), the one way the product morphs words: the box takes the wider and taller of the old and new words at once, holds there while the letters cross, and takes the new words' size in one step when the morph has settled; no width or height ever tweens. Every animation of a swap (a letter gliding to its new place, one arriving from 0.95, one leaving to 0.95, a digit rolling in its slot, and their fades) shares one start, `--dur-morph` (180ms) and ease-out. With reduced motion nothing moves and the swap is still not instant: the old words fade out where they stand and the new ones fade in where they lay out, in the same held box, opacity only, over `--dur-morph`. A label with a second wording it is known to take (a button's "Answer" and "Answering…") stands both in one cell as wide as the wider, so it never changes width at all.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion is opt-in. Every travelling transition and keyframe sits under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, and JavaScript motion asks the same question through `motionOk` (`motion/curves.svelte.ts`). With reduced motion, opacity and colour fades still run, pages cross-fade in place over 120ms, heights land at once, folds fade instead of opening, list changes only fade, flights do not fly, and loops stop (an indeterminate spinner keeps turning). Reduced motion means stillness. It does not mean an instant swap.

rules.name: The House Helper Rule
rules.body: Each kind of motion above has one helper, and a component takes it rather than writing its own (paths from `apps/dashboard/src/lib`). Each already keeps the curves, the clocks, interruption and reduced motion these rules ask for.

rules.name: The Quiet Feel Rule
rules.body: Sound and touch accompany a gesture the reader is making; they never announce anything on their own, never stand in for a word or a glyph, and never play for something the reader did not do. Sound is Cuelume (synthesized live, no files), always at its `subtle` emphasis. It is off until the reader turns it on with the Sound switch beside the theme in the rail's footer, and the choice is kept in this browser (`feel.svelte.ts`). Touch is web-haptics: the Vibration API on Android, and on iOS Safari, which has none, the system tick of a switch toggled out of sight. It answers only a finger on a coarse pointer and has no setting. Both libraries load on the first press or key, never with the page, and Cuelume's audio graph is built while idle right after with an inaudible play, so the first cue costs no frame (built on the first real cue it cost the frame that cue landed in: 76ms against 4ms warm). The moments, all in the composer today: Detent (the recall wheel landing on another entry): `select`, rising toward older and falling toward newer, with a `selection` tick. Overshooting past an end is not a detent. Hold (a held press bringing the wheel up): `open`, with a `medium` tap. Open and close (the wheel brought up by a key, and put away unchosen): `open` and `close`, no touch. Take and give back (a queued message's words lifted into the composer, and given back to their bubble): `select` and `close`, each with a `light` tap.

rules.name: The Dark Flips Polarity Rule
rules.body: At night a groove sits below the card (recess-deep is neutral-1) and a lifted thumb sits above it (neutral-6). Dark mode is a second set of lightness decisions, never an inverted light mode, and neither scheme is designed first.

rules.name: The Reserved Hue Rule
rules.body: Crimson, spark yellow, olive and blue mean status, and status only. Progress rings, identity and decoration take `currentColor` or an identity hue. A finished task ring is the one moment a decoration earns a state colour, because by then it is a result (`TaskRing.svelte`).

rules.name: The Coral Is Where You Act Rule
rules.body: Coral marks the action (one per view: the act the view is for, so a view for deciding spends it on the decision), the selected nav row, the focus ring, checked controls, the chosen option and the selection tint. Advice is never coral: the option a writer recommends wears the Recommended badge (Badges and state chips), and when it starts chosen it wears both, the badge for the advice and the coral edge for the pick, so moving the pick moves only the coral. It is never a status: failed is crimson and needs-you is spark, so coral never reads as an alarm and an alarm never reads as a button.

rules.name: The White On Coral Rule
rules.body: Text on coral sits on `action-solid` or `chip-chosen-bg`, the measured fills, never on `brand-solid`. A new coral fill under text is measured to 4.5:1, top gradient stop included, before it ships.

rules.name: The Ink Stays Ink Rule
rules.body: Tooltips and inverted tiles are `ink-solid` with `on-ink`. They are never coral.

rules.name: The Idle Has No Fill Rule
rules.body: An idle session carries no chip. A quiet row means a healthy row, so rest is drawn as nothing.

rules.name: The No Indigo Rule
rules.body: Indigo is never a brand, action or accent hue. Identity hues span the wheel for telling things apart and are never promoted to a brand role.

rules.name: The Glyph, Word, Hue Rule
rules.body: Status is never colour alone. The session status reads glyph, then word, then hue (a Solar duotone glyph, then "Working", "Needs you", "Failed", "Idle", "Sleeping", "Stopped" or "Unreachable"). The activity dot changes shape as well as colour: Needs you pings, Unreachable is hollow, Sleeping is a moon. A board chip carries the word inside its tint.

rules.name: The 500 Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No product text goes above 500; Fredoka's 600 is brand display only. Emphasis is a weight step from 400 to 500 or an ink step, never bold. The prose plugin's 600 to 800 weights are overridden back to 500.

rules.name: The Role, Not Size Rule
rules.body: Text takes a role by what it does. Names, group headings, column heads and badges are label. Sentences and descriptions are body. Timestamps, counts, units and hints are meta. Nobody picks a size and finds a role for it.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: A figure that changes (a count, a price, an age, a percentage) carries `.num` and is set in tabular numerals, so a ticking value never moves its neighbours. Tables get tabular numerals by default. The KPI role always carries `.num`: `type-kpi` is tabular itself, but a component rule that sets the role by the `font` shorthand resets `font-variant-numeric`.

rules.name: The Truncate Inside Rule
rules.body: Text truncates with an ellipsis in an inner span, never on the control or link itself, so the hit area is never clipped. In a row, the name gives way first and the meta line keeps one line.

rules.name: The Row Dress Rule
rules.body: A list row has at most four dresses, and each part takes the one for its job: the row's name is label in `ink-row` (`ink-subtle` when it is a state standing in for a name); the thing itself (a comment's words, a message) is body in `ink-strong`; facts about it (age, counts, place, the last reply) are meta in `ink-muted`, with a speaker's name inside such a line at 500; an unread fact steps to `ink-strong`, a coral word takes `brand-ink`, and a state that the row's mark already draws takes no word at all.

rules.name: The Mark Line Rule
rules.body: Words set beside a mark (an icon, a glyph, an avatar, a status dot, a keycap) have their x-height's middle on the mark's middle, within half a pixel, in every engine. Centring a line box does not do it: Figtree's ascent and descent sit unevenly about its x-height and Blink floors the half-leading, so a centred 13px label sat 0.3px below its mark in Blink and 1.25px below in WebKit and Gecko. The mark line recipe (app.css) trims each run of words to its x-height band (`text-box: trim-both ex alphabetic`) and pads back the room the trim took, half above and half below, so the run keeps its line's height and centring lands on the x-height. The kit's rows draw it by their own class (option and tray chips, menu items, segments, rail lines, and the button, badge and toggle); any other row takes `.mark-line`. Its words are elements, never bare text beside the mark. A box on the line (a mark's tile, a chevron's cell, a pill) says so with `data-box`. A control that holds nothing but marks (an icon-only button, a link that is only its glyph) is a box too and says `data-box`, centred as one, its glyph on the line's middle within half a pixel; the kit's button given an icon and no label says it on its own. The recipe never finds a box by what it holds: a `:has()` there made every element on the page a selector anchor, and every press restyled the root and the line of ancestors under it. A control's words are an element of their own, and a line that sets a mark in running text says `.mark-text`. A run that truncates clips with `overflow: clip`, never `hidden`, which Gecko does not trim. A run is a block: the trim reaches no flex, grid or table container (CSS Inline 3), which keeps its whole line and takes the padding on top, so a run whose words stack or swap (a label and its reason, two wordings in one cell) holds that layout inside it, and a row of its own on the line says `data-box`. A run that stands alone, such as a pill's own words or a grid cell's label, takes `.mark-text`. A mark beside words that wrap sits in a `.mark-cell`, one line tall at the top of a flex-start row, never nudged down with a margin. A mark set in running text sits on `vertical-align: middle`, and its row says so with `<!-- mark-line: why -->` directly above it, as does any row whose mark is not beside its words. `bun run check` enforces all of this (apps/dashboard/scripts/mark-line-check.ts).

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: On a phone or a coarse pointer every text field renders at 16px (a floor in the last cascade layer, `overrides`, so no utility takes a field under it), because iOS Safari zooms into any field under 16px.

rules.name: The Title Bars Follow Liquid Glass Rule
rules.body: The owner: "this language for titlebars should be scrpaped from all future design, apple's HIG and liquid glass has revised the titlebar model significantly". Every bar that heads a surface (the top bar, a page, a pane, a side panel or column, a sheet, the peek, the artifact panel, a canvas's band) follows Apple's toolbar model as Liquid Glass revised it, on the web, the phone's web and the native app alike (HIG, Toolbars, updated for Liquid Glass 2025-12-16: developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/toolbars): One bar, one row. A surface has one bar, and its title and controls share one line. Facts about the surface (its place, a path, an id, a date, a count, its ask, what it is doing) are content: drawn or said in the surface, or left out. A title stacked over a line of facts beside one row of buttons is the shape this rule retires (the owner, on a project's head: "on the left you have two rows but on the right u have 1 row of buttons"). A title only where it helps. "If titling a toolbar seems redundant, you can leave the title area empty." A side panel or column the person opened by its name (Caw's column, the Comments rail, an inspector) carries no title: its title area stays empty and its actions float over its content (the owner, on Caw's column: "literally useless tiltebar that says nothing, use apple's liquid glass-style HIG floating actions"). Where a title helps, it is the view's own name, short: "Aim for a word or short phrase that distills the purpose of the window or view, and keep the title under 15 characters long so you leave enough room for other controls." It is never the app's name ("Don't title windows with your app name"), an id, a path, a breadcrumb of section names joined by `·` or `›`, or the name of a section the rail already shows chosen. A place shown as a place. Where a surface lives on one machine or in one folder and that matters to it, the place is drawn as a place: the machine as its OS mark and its name, as a control in a group or a fact in the content. A path is never printed in a bar. No bar ground. A bar draws no fill, hairline or shadow of its own: "Reduce the use of toolbar backgrounds and tinted controls. … use the content layer to inform the color and appearance of the toolbar, and use a ScrollEdgeEffectStyle when necessary to distinguish the toolbar area from the content area." The content runs to the surface's top edge, and where it scrolls under the controls the scroll edge effect parts them: the content blurs and fades under the bar ("Scroll edge effects further enhance legibility by blurring and reducing the opacity of background content", HIG, Materials), in from the first scroll and absent at rest, as the transcript's head dissolves into its tab. The folder tabs' shelf is the tab strip's own ground, not a bar's. Floating groups of bare symbols. A bar's controls stand in at most three groups, leading, centre and trailing ("Minimize the number of groups. … In general, aim for a maximum of three"). Each group is one capsule of the panel's glass floating over the content, the top bar's trailing group its recipe (Navigation, menus and floating surfaces): Liquid Glass "forms a distinct functional layer for controls and navigation elements … that floats above the content layer" (HIG, Materials). Its items are bare symbols with no border or fill of their own until hovered or pressed ("Prefer system-provided symbols without borders. … Borders (like outlined circle symbols) aren't necessary because the section provides a visible container"), each named for the screen reader and in its tooltip. A control takes words only where no symbol says it ("except for actions like edit that aren't well-represented by symbols"), in a group of its own ("Keep actions with text labels separate"). Leading holds going back and the title; centre the view's mode or switch; trailing what acts on the view, then More, then the prominent action, with Close after it where the surface closes. One prominent action, trailing. At most one control in a bar is prominent: the one act the view is for, on the coral `action-surface` (Send on a page of picks, Done on a form). A view whose purpose is deciding puts its coral on the decision; Ask Caw takes it only on a view whose purpose is asking him. "Only specify one primary action, and put it on the trailing side of the toolbar." Colour on the glass is for that action and for status alone ("reserve it for elements that truly benefit from emphasis, such as status indicators or primary actions. … Refrain from adding color to the background of multiple controls", HIG, Color › Liquid Glass color). Back and Close are symbols. Back is the chevron-left symbol alone and Close the close symbol alone, each named in its tooltip and for the screen reader by where it goes ("Back to Board"), never a button whose words say Back, Close or the page it returns to: "Prefer the standard symbols for each, and don't use a text label that says Back or Close."

rules.name: The Frame Recesses Rule
rules.body: The frame recesses and content never does. The one sanctioned card-in-card is the stat tile's recessed well, which the reference plan calls "a signature move of the design".

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are warm ink taken from the neutral ramp, never `rgba(0,0,0,·)`. The tile's night drop is the one black, at 30%, under a ring of ink.

rules.name: The Night Ring Rule
rules.body: At night a raised surface is told apart from its frame by a 1px inner ring of ink as well as its drop. The ring is part of the shadow token, so a component that takes the token gets it in both schemes without a class.

rules.name: The Concentric Rule
rules.body: A surface nested in another's corner takes the outer radius less the gap between their edges, the outer's edge counted: outer = inner + gap. It binds where the inner corner stands inside the outer's curve, the same gap in from both edges and less than the outer radius. The dialog tray (18px, 6px padding, no edge) holds a 12px body. A menu (12px, 1px edge, 6px padding) holds 5px items. The segmented groove (10px, 3px padding) holds a 7px thumb. The composer shell (12px, 1px edge, 7px inset) holds 4px controls, its radius less its inset and its edge (`c-inset-composer`). A subagent's well (4px padding) holds its 5px rows, so the well is 9px (`inner-well-r`), the rows' `--radius-xs` plus its `--space-1`. Where no radius token is the derived value it is a derived token whose CSS is that sum or difference (`inner-well-r`), never a literal. A container a highlight stands in says it once (design.css `concentric-in`): it declares its outer radius and its inset, edge counted (`r-outer-lg r-inset-c-inset-floating`), and works out the inner radius, max(0, outer less inset); its rows, segments, controls and parts take it corner by corner (`concentric-<own radius>`), keeping their own radius token where no rounded container holds them. The floating surface (menus, selects, popovers, the bottom sheet's rows: `c-inset-floating`), the composer shell (`c-inset-composer`) and the segmented groove (`c-segmented-pad`) declare it. The hover ghost and the selection pill are drawn from their row's four corners and the focus ring follows the row's radius, so all three take the contour of what they mark; a run's part opened at an edge squares those corners, and the pill under it with them. The rows standing at a glide popover's own inset (12px, 1px edge, 7px padding) are 4px (`glide-row-r`). A decision page's pane pads past its radius (14px in a 12px pane), so a mockup's corners stand clear of its curve.

rules.name: The Measured Exception Rule
rules.body: The stat tile keeps the comp's measured radii (a 10px card around a 7px well, 7px in), even though a concentric well would be 3px. A panel keeps the measured 16px shell (`--radius-panel`: the paywall's hero, a decision page's panels), and the smallest marks keep a 2px hair (`--radius-hair`) rather than the 5px that would turn them into dots. Each is a token, never a literal.

rules.name: The Whole Pixel Border Rule
rules.body: A border or an outline is a whole CSS pixel. A browser snaps its width to whole device pixels, so a 1.5px border draws 1px on a 1× screen and on a 3× one. A fractional stroke (the canvas's corner grip, DialKit's easing handles on a decision page, which the kit's page.css redraws over the vendored sheet's 1.5px border) is an inset ring, `inset-ring-(length:--x)`, whose spread is never snapped, or an SVG stroke. `scripts/border-width-check.ts` (in `bun run check`) refuses a fractional border or outline width in a token, a class or a declaration.

rules.name: The Earned Count Rule
rules.body: A count on a control is drawn only above 0: a count of none says nothing. On the web and in the app alike, at 0 the count element is gone and the control's name drops it too. A figure whose 0 is itself the reading (a measurement, a share, a total the control reports rather than a number of things it opens) is not a count.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: The hand feels a control before release, in one of two ways chosen by size. A compact standalone control (a button, an icon button, a chip, a switch, about 44px tall at most) scales to 0.97 over 160ms on ease-out. Anything wide, large or grouped (rows, cards, card heads, tabs in a strip, segments) tints to `surface-pressed` and moves nothing, because a 0.97 scale pulls a 300px row's edge in by 4.5px; `surface-pressed` is the kit Toggle's on step, the step past the hover (by day the hover step is `surface-fill`'s own, so a press in `surface-fill` would read as the hover; night keeps `surface-fill`). A text link dims to 72% opacity. The scale only runs with motion allowed; the tint always runs. The tint outranks a control's own background by specificity (an id's weight through `:is()`), never by an important declaration, which keeps its fade off the compositor.

rules.name: The Hold-To-Select Rule
rules.body: A press that starts inside a text field in a drawer is not captured by the drawer, so iOS hold-to-select and the Paste callout still reach the field. A held press on a context-menu trigger suppresses the platform callout, because our menu answers it.

rules.name: The Empty Starts Work Rule
rules.body: An empty state always offers to start the work that would fill it. Its one action starts a session with Caw that already asks him to create the thing, its words written for him and editable before they go. The owner: "all empty states should have a way to initiate a session that prompts caw to create it". Where Caw can't start, the empty state says why, and offers the way to do it by hand.

rules.name: The Caw Stands On The Axis Rule
rules.body: Caw's mark sits in the 28px lead column only on a row: a list entry, a notice, a Needs-you row. Everywhere else (an empty page, a hero, a setup or pairing card, a panel's empty state, a fault at a surface's centre) he stands on the composition's own axis: centred over what he heads, never pushed to its leading edge. The lead column is the row grid's; carrying it into a page, a head or a hero left him at the left of an empty page. The owner: "also again, why is caw left aligned here? u seem to have left aligned him everywhere for some reason".

rules.name: The Claim Of Nothing Rule
rules.body: An empty state claims there is nothing to show, so it renders only once the data is known to be empty, never while it is still being read. While data loads, the skeleton stands in at the real layout's size, and the first real read replaces it in the skeleton's reveal (a 400ms cross-fade with a 2px cross-blur) rather than as rows arriving.

rules.name: The Real Wait Rule
rules.body: Caw stands in for a wait (loading, reconnecting) only once it has lasted `--dur-wait-grace` (1s; NN/g: no feedback is needed under 1.0s). Until then the area is its plain surface, with no Caw and no line. Once he appears he stays until his enter (his own clip, about 0.8 s) has played, and what arrives waits for that, so he is never cut off mid-entrance. After that what arrives lands at once under its own `--dur-fade` cross-fade and he is gone within `--dur-fade` from any drawing, his still included: he holds the drawing he is on and fades out (opacity to 0, scale to `--leave-scale`, `--ease-out`), so nothing that has arrived sits under a looping Caw. No exit is drawn. A status change is the same leave, then the new status coming in: by its drawn enter, on every drawing of which he is wholly inside the 3.5% action-safe line or not there at all, or where it has none by a fade up from `--leave-scale` over `--dur-pop` on `--ease-out`; nothing waits for a loop to end (assets/mascot/README.md, Contract). Under Reduce Motion he fades over `--dur-fade`, opacity only. Web: SessionSurface's detail area; Apple: `CawWaiting`.

rules.name: The Composer Layer Rule
rules.body: Nothing that comes out of the composer moves the transcript (owner: "WHY WOULD ANYTHING THAT COMES OUT OF THE COMPOSER EVEN MOVE THE TRANSCRIPT"). The slash and @ menu, the delegate tray's "+N" and failures shelf and its chip panel, the plan its ring opens, the recall wheel and the grown shape are layers of the composer's dock over the transcript's foot, anchored to what opened them, in no flow and never a size the transcript is told: its box, its scroll and its rows hold still to the pixel while one opens or closes, by construction (probe-kit `composer-layers`). The shelf and the plan are the menu's floating surface across the composer's width, a `space-2` step over the tray row, as tall as what they hold up to the room under the dock's top; each comes in on one `@starting-style` transition (`--dur-pop`, drawer curve, from its foot), which iOS 27.2 Safari applies to an element just added (probe-kit `ios-safari-motion`, 2026-10-23), and leaves by `popOut` over `--dur-exit`. While one stands open, the transcript's foot stands solid under it across the pane (`layer-ground`: `surface-recess`, the foot fade's own, up to the layer's foot, then dissolving over `space-8` under the layer), fading in and out on `transition-fade-show`/`-hide`: the tray row has no surface of its own, so a row scrolled behind would otherwise show as a sliver of a line in the `space-2` step, cut mid-glyph by the layer's foot. Rows pass behind the layer and the tray row as they pass behind the pill, whole or not at all.

rules.name: The Composer Touch Rule
rules.body: The textarea sits above its label's touch area, so a press on the text lands on the field itself and iOS hold-to-select and Paste reach it.

rules.name: The One Target Rule
rules.body: On a page in Comment mode, coral is the target and nothing else, and no mark on the page is wider than 1px.

rules.name: The Peer Rule
rules.body: Approve and Deny are peers: the same size (`sm`, 30px; 44px of touch area on a coarse pointer), the same label type, the same fill, the same edge, and neither is ever made the more inviting. Why the rule exists (4ca69663): the operator answers under time pressure, often from a phone, and a rushed thumb must not grant when it meant deny. They take one form on every surface (Caw's panel, the transcript's permission card `transcript/Prompt.svelte`, the peek's answer row `PeekPane.svelte`): apart and untinted. Deny and Approve stand at opposite ends of their row, the row's full width between them and never less than `--space-8`, no third control in that gap, so distance guards the thumb. Both take the one recessed fill (`surface-recess`) and one 1px `border-button-outline` edge, and their glyphs (a cross, a tick) and labels are `ink-strong`; they read apart by glyph, word and place, never by hue. No status fill or status ink touches either (The Reserved Hue Rule; the owner, on a red and a green button under a yellow card: "yellow card on red and green buttons i'm going to VOMIT"). Neither the fill nor the edge changes under the pointer, so the hand's last move never makes one brighter. In Caw's panel the pair's row is the row's last line: Deny on the text column's start, Approve on the trailing edge.

rules.name: The Consequential Grant Rule
rules.body: A standing grant ("Always allow … for …") is a wider grant than the request, so it is kept apart: under a 32px break and a hairline, after a sentence saying what it would allow, and drawn in the warning tint with warning ink, a shield glyph and a real edge. It is the most salient control on the card on purpose. Above the answer row the card says who asks (its title), what will happen and to what (one strong line), and how much changes; then the change itself, open (the transcript's diff, at most `c-ask-diff-share` of the screen tall, scrolling inside), and the other input fields in a recess well, each value scrolling past 200px. Nothing is behind a disclosure: a grant is made on what it changes.

rules.name: The Solar Duotone Rule
rules.body: Every product icon is Solar's bold-duotone cut, imported through `$lib/icons.ts`: one face for the whole product. The duotone's second layer is the same `currentColor` at 50% opacity. A status glyph keeps its hue (`status-*-glyph`) at that 0.5 and holds 3:1 or more as a whole on the surfaces it sits on, so a row's state reads in colour at a glance (9ca3b2154). Chevrons and arrows (`alt-arrow-*`, `arrow-*`) use Solar's linear cut because they are glyphs, not marks. Close, Plus and Tick are local glyphs drawn to Solar's 24px grid with a 1.5 linear stroke and round caps, and Minus is Solar's bare `minus-linear` in the same grammar. The Tick is also the done glyph (a finished step), in `status-done-glyph`, never Solar's `check-circle`. An icon is the glyph alone: no circle, square, squircle or box stands round a Solar glyph, so a `*-circle`, `*-square` or boxed cut is never used where Solar ships the bare one (sort is `sort-from-top-to-bottom`, not the squircled `sort`), and where Solar ships only a contained cut a container-less glyph is drawn in Solar's style, as Info's "i", the MCP plug and a dotted ring drawn in Solar's style for Not yet are (the owner, 10-24: "u need to draw similar style icons that are without their containers").

rules.name: The Caret Rule
rules.body: A text field's focus indicator is its caret ("When text fields receive focus, a vertical bar is displayed in the field, indicating that the user can insert text", WCAG 2.2 Understanding 2.4.7, w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html). No text field, editor or search strip ever draws the coral focus ring, by a key or by a press: a browser matches `:focus-visible` on any focus of a text field, so a ring there stands the whole time it is typed in. A field with a frame of its own steps that frame's 1px border from `border-control` to `border-control-strong` (3:1, WCAG 1.4.11) while its text has focus, on the frame's own radius (`field-edge`: on the field, or on the frame round a borderless editor). A field that is the whole surface (Find's strip, the composer) shows its caret and nothing else. Under forced colours a text field keeps a transparent outline the system paints (Tailwind's `outline-hidden`).

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: Every control (a button, a tab, a row, an option, a handle, a select, a link) shows one ring on keyboard focus only, on `:focus-visible`: a 2px solid outline in `focus-ring`, 2px outside the element. A press on a button shows none. List rows, tabs, options, a select and anything flush against a container or inside a clipping scroller carry the ring inset on their own border box instead, so it never stacks on a border or gets cut. The ring is for focus alone: nothing that is a selection or a mode borrows its colour or its shape (an open comment's pin is marked by its open card, never by a ring; its pill wears the ring only while the keyboard has it, and a modifier held alone is no keyboard use), which take the selected marks instead (`selected-bg` and `selected-ink`, the chosen option's `brand-solid` edge, a page mode's 1px `seam`, a selected canvas frame's label in `selected-ink` and its 1px `border-control-strong` edge). The ring's colour is set at rest, so focus only switches it on. A scroller brings a focused control into view with room for its ring. Pointer focus on a control shows nothing.

rules.name: The 44 Touch Rule
rules.body: On a coarse pointer every control's tappable area reaches 44×44 through a transparent `::after` (`.touch-hit`, WCAG 2.5.8), while its drawn size and the layout stay the same. Where neighbours sit closer, `--hit-gap-x` and `--hit-gap-y` stop each area at the midpoint so areas never overlap; clusters open their gap on touch (8 to 14px for a row's controls, to 16px in the top bar). A text field's area lies under the field (`.hit-under`): the field takes its own presses, so a finger places its caret and selects its words, and the area takes only the room round it. A scroller that would clip the areas pads into an equal negative margin. Menu items and nav rows are 44px tall on touch. One exception: a chip set in running text (ui/chip `inline`: a session, mention or skill in the composer or the transcript) takes its line's height as its hit area, as a link does, because a 44px area there would cover the lines above and below it. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 exempts it: "Inline: The target is in a sentence or its size is otherwise constrained by the line-height of non-target text" (w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum). Every other chip keeps its 44px under a finger.

rules.name: The 24 Pointer Rule
rules.body: On a fine pointer, a control drawn smaller than 24×24 reaches 24px through `.pointer-hit`, with the same midpoint stops. `--hit-scale` keeps the area at 24px on screen inside a zoomed canvas.

dos: Do take every colour, radius, type role, spacing step, curve and duration from the tokens in `design/tokens/cawco.tokens.json`. Add a token there and run `bun run tokens` before adding a one-off value.
Do keep the action coral with its top-highlight gradient, and spend other hue only on status, identity and threshold data.
Do check every change in both schemes; neither is the default.
Do measure white on any new coral fill to 4.5:1, top gradient stop included.
Do recess the frame and raise the content; the stat well is the only card-in-card.
Do say status with a glyph or a word before hue, and draw idle as no chip at all.
Do set every changing figure in tabular numerals (`.num`), and keep weights at 400 and 500.
Do use Solar bold-duotone for every product icon, linear only for chevrons and arrows, at 12, 16 or 20px, each the glyph alone with no circle, square or box round it.
Do make a compact control scale to 0.97 on press and a wide or grouped one tint to `surface-pressed`, the step past the hover, so a press never reads as hovered.
Do give every touch control a 44×44 area and every small pointer target a 24×24 area without changing the drawn size.
Do enter on ease-out over 260 to 280ms and leave over 160ms; move things already on screen on ease-in-out.
Do carry shared objects across a change, and reflow lists rather than letting rows jump.

Do take the house helper for each kind of motion: `morph()` for a size tween, `reflow()` for a list, `unfold` for a disclosure, `NsPopoverGroup` for a popover glide, `fluid-tabs` or the harness `Rail` for a tab switch (The House Helper Rule).

Do design each flow from the four questions of The Stay In Context Rule, sized to the decision: in place for a light one, the affected things named for a heavy one, and every result taken from the system's word.

Do keep work that outlives its surface through a reload and a dismissal: the surface back open at the same step, the work parked in one persistent place with live progress, one press back to it, and every failure said in the error formula with a way on (The Work Outlives Its Surface Rule).

Do open what asks or shows in the page, with the rest still live (The Open Page Rule). Draw facts that have a shape (The Show Don't Tell Rule), and give every empty state the start of Caw's work on it (The Empty Starts Work Rule).
Do put every travelling motion under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` (or `motionOk` in script), and keep fades for reduced motion.
Do show a skeleton at the real layout's size while data loads, and the empty state only once the data is known to be empty.
Do keep sound off until the reader turns it on, play every cue at the subtle emphasis for a gesture the reader made, and give touch only to a finger (The Quiet Feel Rule).
Do keep Approve and Deny as equal peers at opposite ends of their row, with the standing grant set apart below.

Do draw every bar as one row on the content's own ground: a short title only where it helps, at most three floating glass groups of bare symbols, one prominent action trailing, Back and Close as symbols (The Title Bars Follow Liquid Glass Rule).
donts: Don't use coral for a status, crimson or spark for an action, or introduce indigo anywhere as a brand or accent hue.
Don't use a hue for decoration, or use crimson, spark yellow, olive or blue for anything but status.
Don't set text on `brand-solid`, turn a tooltip or ink tile coral, or put spark, paper or crow ink in product chrome.
Don't set product text in Fredoka, or code in anything but JetBrains Mono with ligatures off.
Don't write a token value in `app.css` or a component, or edit the generated `tokens.css`.
Don't set any text above weight 500, or pick a size without a role.
Don't use `rgba(0,0,0,·)` shadows; shadows come from the warm ink tints.
Don't use an ease-in curve, or let an exit run longer than its entrance.
Don't keep an arrived surface moving: no pulse or attention loop on anything that is not live work.

Don't send the reader away from where they asked, show a result the system hasn't confirmed, drop their state when something fails, or copy one flow's parts onto another that doesn't ask the same questions.
Don't let a reload, ×, Esc or a press outside cancel or lose work a surface started, or tell a failure in a toast that leaves on a timer.
Don't play a sound or a tap to announce something, or make one the only sign that something happened.

Don't draw the coral ring on a text field, editor or search strip (The Caret Rule), draw a control's focus as a box-shadow or a background, stack a ring on a border, or give a selection or a mode the ring's shape.
Don't truncate on the control or link itself, which clips its hit area.
Don't render a text field under 16px on a phone or a coarse pointer.
Don't swap Solar for another icon set or for SF Symbols, or drop the duotone layer.
Don't use pill-shaped buttons; full rounding is for state pills, switches and dots.
Don't put a third control between Approve and Deny, or make one more salient than the other.
Don't show an empty state while data is loading, or claim zero while the hub connection is not live.

Don't use a `group-has-*` utility anywhere in the dashboard: one such rule in the sheet makes every element put into the page restyle the whole rail, 20ms and more, whether its group is on the page or not. Style from a state the component sets on itself or its group (`group-data-*`), or from a sibling. `grep -rn "group-has-" apps/dashboard/src` finds none.
